stories.headline: Brent crude tops $110 as fresh attacks in Saudi raise concerns over oil supplies
stories.deck: Oil prices surged past $110 a barrel as Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia raised alarms. The US took precautionary measures by evacuating diplomats' families from the kingdom amid escalating security issues. Simultaneously, US crude inventories dropped sharply, while distillate stocks showed an unexpected increase. Heightened threats to energy supplies from Iran have intensified concerns over…
stories.bodyText:
Oil prices edged higher on Thursday, with Brent crude trading above $110 a barrel. The rise came after fresh Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia prompted US to order some diplomats and their family members to leave American missions in the Kingdom.
At the same time, concerns over shipping safety and oil supplies in the region also persisted.
WTI crude was trading at $98.05, up 90 cents or 0.93%, while Brent crude stood at $110, up $1.15 or 1.06%.
US officials told Reuters that the state department also plans to withdraw family members from several other American missions in the region.
The latest security concerns followed a series of attacks by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis on Wednesday. At least one person was killed and eight others wounded in an attack on a civilian airport in Dammam. A drone attack on a Saudi oil field killed two people.
Explosions were also reported in Sirik, in southern Iran, on Wednesday. Iranian media said that the nature and origin of the blasts were unknown.
Shipping risks extend beyond Strait of Hormuz
The threat to energy supplies has extended to maritime routes beyond the Strait of Hormuz. Kpler data showed at least 18 attacks on shipping over the past two weeks.
LSEG analysts warned that Iran was targeting tankers further afield, including in the Gulf of Oman. Such attacks were jeopardising Gulf crude loadings and ship-to-ship transfers that support regional loadings.
Iran's leadership also issued fresh statements amid the tensions. Foreign minister Abbas Araqchi told the Financial Times on Wednesday that Iran was fully prepared to defend itself. President Masoud Pezeshkian told state media that the US could not expect dialogue while blockading and threatening Iran.
US crude inventories fall, distillate stocks rise
US crude inventories declined by 3.06 million barrels last week to 412.5 million barrels, according to data released by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) on Wednesday. The fall was greater than the 820,000-barrel draw expected by analysts in a Reuters poll.
Distillate inventories, which include diesel and heating oil, increased by 1.68 million barrels to 104.3 million barrels during the week. Analysts had expected these stockpiles to fall by 1.16 million barrels, EIA data showed.
Separately, the Trump administration is offering to loan up to nearly a third of the US emergency heating oil reserve, which holds one million barrels. The department of energy announced the move on Wednesday as the administration seeks to contain prices that have risen amid diesel shortages linked to the wars in Iran and Ukraine.
Elsewhere, Russian President Vladimir Putin met US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine. The meeting came as Washington renewed efforts to end Europe's bloodiest conflict since World War Two.
The Kremlin said Putin had agreed to resume US-mediated peace talks with Ukraine as soon as next month. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy backed the proposed talks and said he hoped they would begin as soon as possible.

stories.headline: Controversy erupts after ‘protest’ photographs by Priyanka Gandhi’s son allegedly get removed from Bikaner House exhibition
stories.deck: “Five hours ago, the Bikaner House Management forced me to remove the bulk of the artworks displayed in my show 'No Idea Is Final”, which opens this evening at 7 p.m.. The photos were of the youth protests in Delhi. Apparently the content is objectionable,” says Raihan Vadra
stories.bodyText:
Controversy erupted after visual artist and photographer Raihan Vadra, son of Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, took to social media on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) and alleged that the management of Bikaner House has removed many of his photographs documenting recent protests and youth movements in India.
Titled “No Idea Is Final”, the exhibition featured wildlife photography, abstract art and pictures documenting recent youth movements in India.
In a post on Instagram, Mr. Vadra wrote, “Five hours ago, the Bikaner House Management forced me to remove the bulk of the artworks displayed in my show 'No Idea Is Final”, which opens this evening at 7 p.m.. The photos were of the youth protests in Delhi. Apparently the content is objectionable.”
He further alleged that the authorities also directed him to remove two photos of the Tiranga.
“I have refused. I will not take down a picture of the Indian flag,” he said, adding that the show will go on in part for now, and he will find another venue and display the entire collection of protest photos.
According to reports, Mr. Vadra was told by the organisers, that it was not the appropriate time to display “such images”.
He argued that a detailed proposal and outline of the exhibition was shared well in advance with the management.
Responding to the development, Congress MP and chairman media and publicity department Pawan Khera questioned the “offence” in clicking protest.
“When even the Tricolour isn’t safe from the censor’s scissors, perhaps the problem isn’t the art. It’s the regime,” he wrote on X.
He added that the photographs merely documented protests, and not one was derogatory or inflammatory.
“Imagine a government so threatened by ideas that not just protests, but even photographs of protests — and the Tricolour itself — have become intolerable. The end must be close,” he said.
The Hindu reached out to the Resident Commissioner, Bikaner House, Rohit Kumar, to seek a response on the issue, but he neither responded to calls nor texts.
Published - October 22, 2026 12:00 am IST

stories.headline: Namma Metro Phase 3: Karnataka issues third land acquisition notification for Orange Line package
stories.deck: Dated October 16, 2026, and published in the Karnataka State Gazette, the notification identifies properties measuring a total of 13,409.05 sq. m. across 11 entries
stories.bodyText:
The Karnataka government has issued a preliminary notification for the additional acquisition of land required for Package 1 of Namma Metro Phase 3, also known as the Orange Line, between J.P. Nagar 4th Phase and the Mysuru Road side of the corridor. This is the third land acquisition notification issued for the package.
Dated October 16, 2026, and published in the Karnataka State Gazette, the notification identifies properties measuring a total of 13,409.05 sq. m. across 11 entries. It provides details of the properties proposed for acquisition, including identification numbers, survey numbers, land extent and information on existing structures.
The properties are located in Kaggalipura, Jaraganahalli and other localities along the proposed metro alignment.
“This is the third land acquisition notification issued for Package 1 of Corridor 1 of Namma Metro Phase 3. The notification is part of the land acquisition process for the 44.65-km Phase 3 project, which will expand Bengaluru’s metro network with 31 stations across two corridors,” a Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) official said.
Meanwhile, more than two years after the project received approval, BMRCL recently invited expressions of interest from Indian and international consultancy firms to serve as the General Consultant for Phase 3. The consultant will provide technical and project management support for the development of both corridors.
Corridor 1 will run 32.15 km from J.P. Nagar 4th Phase to Kempapura and have 22 stations, while Corridor 2 will cover 12.50 km between Hosahalli and Kadabagere, with nine stations.
JICA assistance sought
BMRCL has applied for a Japanese Official Development Assistance loan of ¥102.48 billion from the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) to part-finance the two corridors.
“The proposed JICA loan will meet only a portion of the overall project cost, while BMRCL will arrange the balance funding. Consultancy appointments and procurement for components financed through the loan will be carried out in accordance with JICA guidelines,” the official said.
The General Consultant will review engineering designs, prepare and finalise tender documents, assess bids, and assist with contract negotiations. Once construction begins, the consultant will also monitor quality standards, workplace safety and environmental compliance, coordinate contractors’ work, and support testing and commissioning before the lines become operational.
Phase 3 is expected to improve connectivity across Bengaluru and ease congestion on busy stretches, particularly along the western Outer Ring Road, Magadi Road and other major arterial roads.
The project also envisages integration with existing and under-construction metro stations, BMTC bus terminals, Indian Railways stations and proposed suburban rail stations being developed by K-RIDE.
Multi-modal integration facilities are planned at JP Nagar 4th Phase, JP Nagar, Kamakya, Mysuru Road, Sumanahalli, Peenya, BEL Circle, Hebbal, Kempapura and Hosahalli. According to officials, these facilities are intended to enable seamless transfers between different modes of public transport and improve access to the expanded metro network.

stories.headline: ‘Racial attack’ by Delhi influencer on tribal youth roils Tripura
stories.deck: In Tripura, a controversial video featuring influencer Amir Shokeen allegedly mocking a tribal youth has ignited political backlash. Leaders throughout the region voiced their outrage, labeling the incident a racial attack and pushing for swift action. CM Manik Saha has directed the Tripura DGP to collaborate with Delhi Police for a comprehensive investigation.
stories.bodyText:
AGARTALA/NEW DELHI: Political parties in Tripura closed ranks Wednesday over the alleged racial harassment in Delhi of a tribal youth from Gomati district and demanded legal action against social media influencer Amir Shokeen after a video purportedly showing him taunting the young man over his ethnicity circulated online.
The clip, which surfaced Tuesday evening, purportedly shows Shokeen asking the youth if he is the "president" of a neighbouring country. He allegedly also mocks Tripura when the man responds he is Indian.
CM Manik Saha of BJP directed the Tripura DGP to coordinate with Delhi Police and ensure a proper probe. CPM state secretary and lead-er of the opposition Jitendra Chaudhury demanded Shokeen apologise.
"Establish a precedent that is both resounding and unmistakable, ensuring no one ever dares insult Tripura and the Tiprasa community again," he said.
Congress MLA Sudip Roy Barman called for a joint protest in Delhi. "This type of attitude is intolerable," he said.
After TIPRA Motha chief Pradyot Kishore Debbarman called on the party's youth and students' wings to act, Youth Tipra Federation lodged a complaint accusing Shokeen of hate speech and defamatory remarks.
"Shokeen made crude and vulgar remarks..., calling him 'Chinese' and made fun of our state's name," said James Debbarma, general sec-retary of Youth Tipra Federation and an elected member of the Tripura tribal areas autonomous district council.
Members of Twipra Students' Federation plan to meet the Delhi Police commissioner Thursday. "We are trying to identify the boy who was harassed and file a complaint," said general secretary Hamalu Jamatia.
Shokeen has put out a video on Facebook claiming it was scripted. He said the target of his alleged abuse was an acquaintance who worked at a friend's cafe in Ahmedabad. "I did not intend to insult the people of Tripura, and I apologise if my words hurt anyone," he said.

stories.headline: Landslide derails locomotive in southern Keralam, disrupts train services
stories.bodyText: Thiruvananthapuram: A landslide near the Parassala railway station in this southern Keralam district early on Thursday derailed the locomotive of the Bilaspur-Tirunelveli Express, disrupting train services in the Neyyattinkara-Parassala section, the railways said here. . The incident occurred at 2:19 am when Train No. 22619 Bilaspur-Tirunelveli Express was stopped near Parassala following the landslide. .Kerala PCC guards leaders against Oommen Chandy sentiments being dragged to attack V D Satheesan. The locomotive was found derailed after the train stopped at the location, the railways said. . "All passengers and railway staff are safe," the Southern Railway said in a statement. . A relief locomotive was immediately arranged to move the train, while an accident relief train (ART), along with personnel and materials, was rushed to the site to carry out restoration work and resume train services, it said. . Three trains were held en route due to the disruption. . The Tambaram-Thiruvananthapuram Central Special was held at Eraniel, the Madurai-Punalur Express was held at North Panakudi and the Tambaram-Thiruvananthapuram Central Amrit Bharat Express was held at Nanguneri. . The departure of five other trains -- the Kanniyakumari-Mangaluru Central Parasuram Express, the Nagercoil Junction-Punalur Passenger, the Thiruvananthapuram North-Nagercoil Junction Passenger, the Punalur-Kanniyakumari Passenger and the Thiruvananthapuram Central-Tambaram Express -- was delayed. . The Guruvayur-Chennai Egmore Express and the Pune-Kanniyakumari Express were also expected to be delayed, the Southern Railway said. .Cong, Left, CJP protests in Delhi for 'regime change', not over CEC, SIR: Keralam BJP chief.Alpassi Arattu: Keralam airport halts flights for 5 hours for religious procession. Restoration work is underway in the affected section and train services are expected to remain disrupted until the work is completed. . The incident occurred amid a spell of heavy rain in the region. . The India Meteorological Department (IMD) had issued an orange alert for Thiruvananthapuram district on Wednesday, warning of very heavy rainfall, and a yellow alert for October 22 to October 25, forecasting heavy rain.

briefs.headline: Trump again targets offshore wind, risking deal to speed approvals of new energy projects
briefs.deck: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, a Rhode Island Democrat, warned that the administration now risks derailing a legislative effort to speed up permitting reviews for new energy and infrastructure projects
briefs.bodyText:
The Trump administration is asking a federal judge to let it reconsider a major federal permit granted for a large offshore wind farm, making it the fourth project the Republican leadership has targeted in recent months.
The Interior Department wants to reconsider its own approval for the "construction and operations plan" for the New England Wind project off Massachusetts. The plan was approved in 2024 during the Biden administration. The Justice Department said in a filing on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) that the Court should send the permit back to Interior, because the plan was approved despite major adverse impacts.
Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, a Rhode Island Democrat, warned that the administration now risks derailing a legislative effort to speed up permitting reviews for new energy and infrastructure projects. The Senate reached a bipartisan deal in September on a permitting bill, which has not yet been voted on.
"This is how you blow up a permitting deal," he said in a statement on Wednesday (October 21, 2026).
The Trump administration is using executive orders, agency actions and the courts to try to stop the development of offshore wind, a technology that President Donald Trump has attacked as "ugly" and unreliable compared to fossil fuels such as coal and natural gas. Officials started buying back offshore wind leases after federal judges blocked its efforts to stop construction on five major East Coast projects.
The Interior Department also wants to reconsider its prior approval of the construction and operations plan for Revolution Wind, a wind farm for Rhode Island and Connecticut that has finished construction, and for the Maryland Offshore Wind Project, which has not yet begun construction.
In August, a judge granted the administration's request to reconsider the permit for the stalled New Jersey project Atlantic Shores. That project had been halted soon after Mr. Trump returned to office because co-owner Shell walked away from it.
Last year, a federal judge said the Trump administration could reconsider the permit granted to the Massachusetts project SouthCoast Wind days before the President's inauguration to a second term.
Pasha Feinberg, an offshore wind strategist at the Natural Resources Defence Council, said the Trump administration's attacks on offshore wind are escalating at a time when Americans are struggling with surging utility bills.
"It's long past time for the Trump administration to realise its war on clean energy is backfiring," Mr. Feinberg said.
The National Ocean Industries Association, which represents offshore industries including oil and wind, said it's concerned about the uncertainty that comes with reopening federal approvals for offshore energy projects, particularly those already under construction or in operation.
"The Senate has made meaningful progress on deep reforms that would provide greater certainty for energy projects across the board," said the association's president, Erik Milito. The administration's actions "underscore why Congress needs to get this done", he said.
The plans for New England Wind call for up to 129 wind turbines that could supply as much as 2,600 megawatts of clean energy to power more than 900,000 homes each year. The developer, Avangrid, declined to comment on Wednesday (October 21, 2026). Construction has not begun.
The project's federal approval was challenged in court by ACK for Whales, a group of Nantucket, Massachusetts, residents who say they are concerned about the negative impacts of offshore wind development. The lawsuit in District Court for the District of Columbia contends that the federal government failed to comply with numerous statutes.
The federal defendants in the case filed a motion on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) stating that remand of the permit is warranted, so Interior could make a new decision. The government also told the Court in 2025 it wanted to reconsider New England Wind's approval.
Interior said in a statement on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) that the latest filing complied with a briefing schedule and was not announcing a policy change. Its position on offshore wind has remained consistent throughout this administration, the statement said.
Avangrid built another wind farm, Vineyard Wind, off the coast of Massachusetts in a joint venture with Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners. Construction finished in March, making it the first project to reach this stage during Mr. Trump's time in office. Vineyard Wind was one of the projects the administration tried to halt construction on, citing concerns over national security.
Published - October 22, 2026 07:12 am IST

briefs.headline: Mumbai Police issue notices to 24 ''X'' accounts over Sabeer Bhatia's documentary
briefs.deck: The notices were issued on October 18, days after the documentary, allegedly containing false and disparaging claims about Prime Minister Narendra Modi and industrialist Gautam Adani, sparked a controversy
briefs.bodyText:
Mumbai Police have issued legal notices to 24 'X' (formerly Twitter) account holders, days after they shared a controversial documentary posted by tech entrepreneur Sabeer Bhatia.
The notices were issued on October 18, days after the documentary, allegedly containing false and disparaging claims about Prime Minister Narendra Modi and industrialist Gautam Adani, sparked a controversy.
The notices stated that cyber police had received a formal complaint alleging that multiple X handles had published highly objectionable content targeting a prominent business conglomerate.
The links mentioned in the notices directed to Mr. Bhatia's X account.
The content allegedly had false, misleading, and disparaging statements and allegations against the company, which were circulated without any factual or lawful basis, causing continuous harm to its reputation, goodwill and public image, the notices said.
The publication of such content violated platform guidelines and constituted offenses punishable under Sections 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of the peace) and 356 (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), they said.
The notices asked the platform and account holders to urgently review the objectionable posts and remove or disable access to the content.
While several account holders complied by deleting the video clips, others publicly shared copies of the police notice on their handles, alleging overreach and terming the action as unjust.
“Mumbai Police asked me to take down certain highly objectionable tweets. I have complied and removed them,” Mr. Bhatia, the Indian-American entrepreneur who co-founded the first free web-based email service Hotmail.com in 1996, said on X.
“The “highly objectionable” tweet merely pointed out alleged corruption at the highest levels of power," he said.
The law enforcement agency apparently found the corruption less objectionable than the act of exposing it, he added.
“When pointing out wrongdoing becomes a greater offense than the wrongdoing itself, who is the law really protecting?”
“I regret to inform the good people of India that their fundamental right to free speech is being curtailed by the government. This government is no longer of the people, by the people, or for the people,” he said.
“I am deeply disappointed. In a nation of 1.45 billion people, citizens are afraid to open their mouths and speak about what they see. How can anyone hope to fix India when fear has silenced its people?” he said on X.
A nation cannot progress when speaking the truth requires courage, Mr. Bhatia said.
Published - October 22, 2026 07:03 am IST

briefs.headline: Andhra Pradesh SEC halts election process for 100 ULBs after Supreme Court order
briefs.deck: SEC will issue an order on the ULB elections on October 22 after obtaining reports from Collectors, District Election and Police authorities
briefs.bodyText:
Andhra Pradesh State Election Commissioner (SEC) Anil Chandra Punetha has ordered that the election process for all 100 Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) for which the notification was issued on October 14 be stopped forthwith in view of the Supreme Court’s directions.
Mr. Punetha, in a late-evening order, said that the SEC would issue an order on the ULB elections after obtaining reports from the Collectors, District Election Authorities and Police Commissioners or Superintendents of Police October 22.
He said the notification for the elections to 13 Municipal Corporations, 87 Municipalities and Nagar Panchayats in the State was issued on October 14 and the nomination process was completed between October 16 to 18, followed by the scrutiny of nominations on October 19.
However, the Supreme Court has directed the SEC to postpone the publication of the final list of candidates for the ULB elections till October 25.
Meanwhile, the SEC was mandated to consider the representations made by the petitioner party (YSRCP) and other candidates, including evidentiary material as well as electronic evidence placed before it and take a decision on the last date for filing nominations wherever it is of the view that candidates were unable to file their nominations due to law and order situation, he said.
Published - October 21, 2026 11:28 pm IST

briefs.headline: U.P. CM Yogi issues directions for strict legal action in cases of land encroachment
briefs.deck: Officials must impose strict legal action on anyone who illegally occupies land or dispossesses vulnerable people, while urging dialogue to resolve familial property disputes and promising swift assistance to victims seeking government benefits or medical treatment, says Uttar Pradesh CM
briefs.bodyText:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) instructed officials that those who illegally occupy someone else’s land or dispossess vulnerable people must not be spared under any circumstances. Mr. Adityanath issued directions during a Janata Darshan held at Gorakhnath Temple in Gorakhpur.
“The Chief Minister instructed officials that those who illegally occupy someone else’s land or dispossess vulnerable people must not be spared under any circumstances. Strict legal action must be taken against them. If a dispute concerning land or property is familial in nature, the concerned parties should be brought together and the matter resolved through mutual dialogue,” reads an official statement.
The Chief Minister added that no one should suffer injustice. Every victim must be assisted with sensitivity. “Those who, for any reason, have been deprived of the benefits of government schemes should be provided with those benefits,” added Mr. Adityanath.
During the Janata Darshan, some people approached the Chief Minister seeking financial assistance for medical treatment. The CM assured them that the government would provide all possible assistance for their treatment. “While forwarding their applications to the officials, the Chief Minister directed that the process of preparing treatment estimates be completed as soon as possible and that the estimates be submitted to the government,” added the official statement.
During the Janata Darshan, the Chief Minister told officials, “Resolving everyone’s problems and bringing public welfare and happiness into citizens’ lives is the government’s commitment. In accordance with this commitment, the resolution of grievances must be ensured by treating every victim with sensitivity,”.
During the Janata Darshan, the Chief Minister met around 200 people. He personally approached the people seated in front of the Mahant Digvijaynath Smriti Bhawan in the temple premises and heard their problems one by one. While forwarding everyone’s applications to the concerned officials and directing them to ensure prompt and satisfactory resolution, he assured the people that the government is committed to resolving the problems of every victim.
Published - October 22, 2026 03:00 am IST

briefs.headline: Current El Nino event could be unprecedented in strength: WMO
briefs.deck: It stated that sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific may rise to 3.8 degrees Celsius above average during November 2026 to January 2027
briefs.bodyText:
The prevailing El Nino conditions over the tropical Pacific could be unprecedented in strength, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) in its new seasonal climate outlook.
It stated that sea surface temperatures in the tropical Pacific may rise to 3.8 degrees Celsius above average during November 2026 to January 2027.
The WMO declares an El Nino when the sea surface temperature anomaly in this region is 0.5 degrees Celsius.
In a statement, WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo said, "This is literally off the monitoring charts that we have used for the past four decades. El Nino will peak towards the end of 2026 but its impacts will be felt long after that."
El Nino is one of the three phases of the El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) — a climate phenomenon characterised by changes in sea temperatures along the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean, accompanied by fluctuations in the atmosphere overhead.
While El Nino is known to have a warming effect over the planet, its opposite phase, La Nina, usually results in a cooling effect. ENSO also has a neutral phase.
A very strong El Nino disrupts normal temperature and rainfall patterns across many regions, according to the WMO.
El Nino can bring severe drought to some regions, heavy rainfall and flooding to others, and increased heat across large parts of the world.
Published - October 22, 2026 06:33 am IST

briefs.headline: Sexual offence charge rocks India's Asian Para Games contingent; swimmer faces ban
briefs.deck: A senior PCI official, who is part of the Indian delegation in Nagoya and who handled the entire situation, confirmed the development to TOI, describing the alleged misconduct as “reprehensible and intolerable” and saying there could be “no justification” for such behaviour by an athlete representing the country on the international stage.”
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The Indian contingent at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya has been left embarrassed after para swimmer Mohammad Shams Aalam Shaikh was detained by Japanese police following allegations of sexually harassing and molesting a female hotel employee. The 40-year-old, once a world No 1 in his event, was sent back to India on Tuesday, a day after the alleged incident, and faces the prospect of a lifetime ban from the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI).
A senior PCI official, who is part of the Indian delegation in Nagoya and who handled the entire situation, confirmed the development to TOI, describing the alleged misconduct as “reprehensible and intolerable” and saying there could be “no justification” for such behaviour by an athlete representing the country on the international stage.”
“Aalam is staring at no less than a lifetime ban for bringing disrepute to the entire Indian delegation participating at the Asian Para Games and for embarrassing the country on the world stage,” the official said.
According to the official, the incident occurred on Monday at the Four Points by Sheraton hotel, where the Indian para swimming team was staying. The female employee was reportedly carrying out housekeeping duties in the swimmer’s room when the alleged misconduct took place.
“The local organising committee (LOC) informed the chef-de-mission’s (CDM) office that an alleged sexual harassment and molestation incident had occurred at the hotel and that an Indian athlete had been detained by the local police,” the official said.
“When we reached the hotel, the police and senior hotel managers were already there. We were told that the athlete had inappropriately touched the female housekeeping staff member, made sexually coloured gestures, attempted to grope her and made sexual advances. She rushed out and informed her superiors. This is what we were told by the police and hotel staff,” the official added.
The official said the delegation apologised to the hotel authorities and the employee. Following the complaint, police detained Shaikh and took him to a local police station. The official said the authorities sought his arrest and that he be formally presented before a court.
The LOC subsequently intervened, with the Indian delegation asked to furnish a written apology to the employee and ensure that the athlete left Japan. Shaikh was moved to another hotel for the night and booked on the first available flight, departing Nagoya at around 2 pm local time on Tuesday, the official said. He was released after the written apology was furnished, according to the official’s account.
“The police authorities had clearly recorded the sexual offence allegation in their formal complaint, in Japanese. We can confirm that since I saw that,” the official said.
The official added the incident had diverted senior Indian officials from the contingent’s ongoing sporting campaign. “Instead of focusing on the Games and our athletes’ performances, we spent several hours at the police station and later at the hotel premises convincing the authorities. We were embarrassed in front of everyone,” the official said.
He added that the employee appeared to be in deep shock when the delegation returned to the hotel. The hotel and LOC, he said, sought updates on the action India would take and warned that they could pursue formal legal proceedings if they were dissatisfied with the response.
The PCI has informed the govt in New Delhi of the proposed action, the official said. After the Games, PCI officials, para swimming administrators and members of the delegation will deliberate on the matter and recommend stringent sanctions to the sports ministry and Sports Authority of India (SAI).
“The CDM’s office has already recommended a lifetime ban. A formal decision will be taken at a meeting in Delhi after we return,” the official said.
Shaikh, who hails from Bihar’s Madhubani district and lives with his family in Mumbai’s Dharavi, was sent home without competing in his scheduled events on Wednesday.
A former world No. 1 in the men’s 100m butterfly (S5) and 50m breaststroke (SB4), according to World Para Swimming records, Shaikh represented India at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta and won 200m breaststroke gold at the Reykjavik International Games last year, setting Indian and Asian records.
The incident comes close on the heels of an Indian hockey umpire and technical official Gurinder Singh Sangha was being sent home from the able-bodied Asian Games in Nagoya following sexual misconduct and harassment complaints by a Malaysian hockey official and a hotel staff member.

briefs.headline: Missiles strike Ukraine's Kyiv: Report
briefs.bodyText: Kyiv: Missiles struck Kyiv in the early hours of Thursday, a Reuters witness said, in another attack on Ukraine's capital after a Russian evening air strike which injured six people and damaged homes, a petrol station and transport equipment. In Russia, in the city of Lipetsk — home to a major steel plant some 400 km (250 miles) south of Moscow — a man was injured as drones hit apartment buildings and a medical facility, Governor Igor Artamonov said on the Telegram messaging app. .Russian strike kills woman, hits Kyiv subway station, mayor says. The strikes come as US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff held talks this week with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Russia's President Vladimir Putin to mediate an end a conflict which began with Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

briefs.headline: 'Much, much bigger leaders than me': Dipke hails Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka after release
briefs.deck: Das and Ranka were released after the expiry of judicial custody in connection with the October 14 protest at Jantar Mantar.
briefs.bodyText:
The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) welcomed the Special Executive Magistrate's order releasing its leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, with founder Abhijeet Dipke calling them "much, much bigger leaders" than him.
CJP's legal head Ratna Singh said the decision should have come earlier.
Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka were released after the expiry of judicial custody in connection with the October 14 protest at Jantar Mantar.
In a social media post, Mr. Dipke expressed his willingness to follow orders of Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka.
"Saurav and Ashu are not just better but much, much bigger leaders than me. Happy to follow your orders, my leaders. Jaan hazir hai!" Mr. Dipke said.
He added a playful remark in Hindi, saying, "Lekin iske baad mere bina garden mein koi akela nahi ghumega!!! (But after this, don't go alone in the garden without me)".
In another post, Mr. Dipke shared a photograph of Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka and captioned it "My leaders".
Earlier, Ms. Singh said, "We welcome the decision. I think this decision should have been taken long ago, but it is not too late".
She said the police had sought a five-day extension of their custody citing an imminent threat, but the defence argued that there was no imminent threat and no call for a protest.
"You cannot take that as an assumption and extend the judicial custody. The SEM has taken that on record," she said.
Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka were initially remanded to five days of judicial custody on October 14 after being detained for allegedly entering the denotified protest site of Jantar Mantar and violating peace bonds. Their custody was extended by two days on October 19.
Asked about the Delhi High Court's observations earlier in the day, Ms. Singh said the judge was entitled to express an opinion, but the CJP did not necessarily agree with it.
"They have given their opinion. It is an observation, an oral observation.”
“There was no discussion on the merits in the Court. We were here today for the release of Saurav and Ashutosh, for which we had been trying for the past week. Finally, that has happened," she said.
Ms. Singh said the team was emotional and eager to meet the two leaders.
"The team is also very emotional right now. They also want to meet them because everyone has not met them for a long time," she said.
She expressed hope that nobody's liberty would be curtailed in the future over issues related to sureties or technical reasons, adding that the release order had been sent and the team hoped to see Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka soon.
Earlier, the High Court declined to interfere with Mr. Das and Mr. Ranka's judicial custody, asking them to await the SEM court's decision and approach the appellate court if their grievance persisted.

stories.headline: Newlywed climbs mobile towers twice in Bengaluru, asks police to trace missing husband
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: A 20-year-old homemaker, newly married, has climbed mobile towers twice since Monday in Madanayakanahalli, near Nelamangala, demanding that police and her family trace her husband, whom she married just 15 days ago.
On Tuesday, 
Ramya
 (name changed) lodged a missing person complaint, alleging that her husband, whom she married on Oct 6, had abandoned her on Oct 18.
Before climbing the towers, Ramya had also sat in the middle of the busy Hosur Road near Parappana Agrahara Sunday night after realising that her husband had deserted her, disrupting traffic. Police took her to a state-run women’s home, but she left Monday morning after her mother visited her.
“On Monday afternoon, she went to her husband’s house in Kuvempunagar, Madanayakanahalli. When she found that he was not there and his mobile phone was switched off, she climbed a mobile tower near the Bangalore International Exhibition Centre. She came down after family members and friends consoled her.
“However, on Tuesday afternoon, she climbed another mobile tower near Makali. This time, she demanded that police and media come to the spot and resolve her problem. We assured her that we would take appropriate action to trace her husband. A journalist from a local media outlet recorded a video and told Ramya that the incident would be aired. She then climbed down,” an investigating officer said.
Police also said there were no valid documents to establish the marriage. When questioned, Ramya claimed that the wedding had taken place on Oct 6 at a friend’s house in Nagavara.

stories.headline: Deleted from Bengal’s SIR rolls, Bengaluru migrants weigh costly trip home
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: As West Bengal begins a mop-up exercise for voters left out of special intensive revision (SIR), migrant workers in Bengaluru fear another financial setback if they have to return home to restore their voting rights. Many said their documents were verified during hearings, but their names were missing from the final rolls.
Tubrahalli and neighbouring areas in the city’s IT corridor are home to thousands of migrant workers employed in construction, domestic work and delivery services. About 13,000 Bengali families live here, said Sharifull Sekh, vice-president of Bengali Kalyani Trust. He estimated that 3,000 had lost their voting rights during SIR.
Residents said they had spent an average of Rs 10,000 each travelling to West Bengal to respond to notices and vote, only to find their names missing from the rolls. The workers said they will go back if called for the mop-up, even if it means losing wages and spending nearly a month’s salary.
Having moved to Bengaluru two to five years ago, many lack permanent residence certificates that could support enrolment here through Form 6. 
Most prefer to reclaim their voting rights in West Bengal.
The deletions have not affected access to ration so far, said Sagari Khatun from Murshidabad, whose seven-year-old son has thalassaemia. “No one has reached out yet. But if they call us even now, I will go and have my voter ID restored,” she said.
Saheb Ali, whose name was flagged for a “logical discrepancy” because his father’s name was spelt differently in official records, said he will temporarily give up construction work, which pays twice as much as he can earn back home, to correct the error. “Everyone in the family but my sister and I were allowed to vote,” he said.
Sheefil Ali Shek’s wife, a domestic worker, also lost her voting rights. “The shock came when she went to the polling booth and her name was not on the roll. We went thrice for SIR hearings and documentation, each time spending Rs 10,000 on transport,” he said.
Anarul Vishyas from Nadia in West Bengal said his hearing was completed and he was told to go back, but his name did not appear in the final rolls. Tea stall owner Adur Ali Shek said several migrant voters faced similar experiences, with documents collected and voters sent home without officials clarifying discrepancies on the spot. Some errors appeared glaring. Jalema Bai (35) was recorded as 60, her husband said. Manowara Kha, one of nine children, was flagged because more than six children were linked to her mother.

stories.headline: Transmen cricket team from Karnataka battles financial barriers ahead of national tournament
stories.bodyText:
In December 2025, a transmen team from Karnataka participated in a national-level cricket tournament for the first time. The odds were stacked against them. Yet the spirited group managed to reach the semifinals, in which teams from five other States participated.
“Participation was the only aim then. The hope was that we would be able to practice more regularly and prepare better for next year’s tournament,” says Aadhityanath, captain of the Karnataka team, which became second runners-up in the 2025 tournament.
The next tournament is scheduled to be held in Punjab in November this year. But their dreams of winning continue to be overshadowed by the struggle to access even basic facilities, such as practice nets and kits.
Multiple expenses
The third edition of the Transgender Persons’ Cricket Tournament is being organised by the Transgender Athletes Foundation and will be held on the Lovely Professional University campus in Punjab.
“A practice net would cost close to ₹1,400 per hour in Bengaluru. Booking nets for full days over several days is beyond our budget,” Aadhityanath says.
Most of the team members work small jobs to earn their livelihood. Some help out in textile shops, some work as cooks, and a few others work with NGOs. The team estimates that it will need ₹2,74,500 to cover the tournament expenses of all 13 players.
Major expenses apart from the nets include cricket kits, medical kits, and travel tickets.
Nets practice important
While Raahi, a Karnataka-based non-profit that works on the rights of the LGBTQIA+ community, helped cover a major portion of the expenses last year, this time the organisation is finding it difficult to offer financial support beyond a limit. The team has been practising occasionally at the grounds of RBANMS College.
“Practising in nets is very different from practising on a rough ground with gravel. Besides, the ground is not always available, making it difficult for us to maintain a consistent practice schedule,” Aadhityanath points out.
“We would like to practice throughout the year. But given the difficulty in accessing nets and gear, this becomes out of the question. Everything comes to a halt soon after a tournament,” he adds.
Talented team
Although the organisers provide train tickets for the team, the longer travel time means players have to take more days off work. Last year, several players reportedly faced difficulties at their workplaces as a result. But most cannot afford flight tickets.
“After last year’s tournament, three of us from the Karnataka team were selected for a national team to take part in the Rashtriya Cricket League that starts on October 22. But one player withdrew due to such difficulties,” Aadhityanath notes.
Amid the difficulties, he is hopeful, though. “It’s a talented team. But many don’t even know we exist. With the right support, we can go a long way. We hope we’ll be able to find that support.”

stories.headline: Bengaluru South City Corporation pilots evening waste collection in five wards
stories.bodyText:
The Bengaluru South City Corporation has introduced evening waste collection on a pilot basis in five wards to address roadside garbage blackspots and make it easier for residents to hand over their waste, Commissioner K.N. Ramesh said on Wednesday. Under the pilot, vehicles collecting wet and dry waste will operate from 5 p.m. to midnight. The initiative covers four wards in the Bommanahalli Assembly constituency and Hongasandra ward.
Mr. Ramesh inspected the evening collection system and said the initiative was aimed at helping residents who are unable to hand over waste to collection vehicles during morning hours because of work and other commitments.
While 160 waste collection vehicles operate in the mornings across the five wards, 20 to 25 autos have been deployed for evening collection. In Hongasandra alone, six vehicles, three each for wet and dry waste, operate in the evening, while 31 autos are deployed in the morning, he said.
Long-standing demand
The pilot initiative may come as a relief to hundreds of residents, as evening waste collection, or twice-a-day collection, has long been a demand across the city.
Residents’ Welfare Associations in south Bengaluru have repeatedly flagged the increase in garbage blackspots in the area. Initially, many argued that households that had previously handed over unsegregated waste to collection vehicles were resorting to littering after Bengaluru Solid Waste Management Limited (BSWML), under the new solid waste management rules, directed collection vehicles not to accept unsegregated waste.
The issue was flagged in localities such as Adugodi, S.G. Palya and along Siddapura Road, where new blackspots were reported recently.
Many residents had also taken to social media, highlighting the need for waste collection during evening hours while pointing to the emergence of garbage blackspots. Similar requests had been made repeatedly to Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda, who had rejected the idea, arguing that accommodating residents’ convenience would effectively require civic authorities to collect garbage throughout the day. He had also said it was not feasible to ask sanitation workers to collect garbage twice a day or appoint additional workers for the purpose.

briefs.headline: Rs 30 lakh gone: Gold, cash stolen from Bengaluru house during polishing work

Bengaluru:
 A house renovation job led to a loss for a family after gold jewellery, weighing 254 grams, and Rs 5 lakh in cash were stolen from a cupboard while polishing work was underway. The house owner suspects the involvement of three labourers, engaged for the work, in the crime.
According to a complaint filed by Mariyappa B, a resident of Padmanabhanagar in Banashankari, he had hired three labourers, identified as 
Shankar
, Nagesh alias Girish and Ramcharan, for the polishing work at his house from Oct 4 to 11.
The theft allegedly took place around 12.30pm on Oct 10, when the family was away from home. However, it came to light only on Oct 18, when they opened the cupboard and found the valuables missing.
The stolen gold jewellery, worth around Rs 25.4 lakh, included seven pairs of bangles, two chains, five rings, three children’s rings, a five-gram coin, a three-gram pendant, two pairs of earrings and a necklace set, the complaint said.

briefs.headline: Fire guts 3BHK flat at in Bengaluru’s Uttarahalli
briefs.deck: No Casualties
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 A fire gutted a flat on the eighth floor of an apartment complex at Uttarahalli Wednesday, with officials suspecting an electrical short circuit as the cause.
The fire department received a call at 11.52 am, and four fire tenders from Hulimavu, Dairy Circle and Banashankari stations rushed to the spot and brought the flames under control. Officials said the fire was confined to the single 3BHK flat in D block of Brigade 7 Gardens. The extent of the loss is yet to be assessed.
A resident of Brigade 7 Gardens, who witnessed the incident, questioned the response. According to the resident, the fire was initially confined to a single room. One or two firefighters, along with a group of residents, tried to douse it from the ground floor, but the water was not reaching the flames. “It was pretty obvious that the water wasn’t reaching the fire, but they kept trying,” the resident said.
By the time the approach was abandoned, the fire had spread to other parts of the flat, and a small explosion in an adjacent room triggered another fire, the resident said. A turntable ladder arrived only towards the end, when little could be saved, the resident claimed.

briefs.headline: Greater Bengaluru Authority receives over 1,500 objections to tree felling for Hebbal Short Tunnel
briefs.deck: The National Green Tribunal restrained the BDA from felling any trees till the hearing in the case challenging tree felling for the project is completed
briefs.bodyText:
The Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) has received more than 1,500 objections to the proposed felling of 1,128 trees for the Hebbal Short Tunnel Project. Meanwhile, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) has restrained the Bangalore Development Authority (BDA) from felling any trees until the hearing of a petition challenging the tree felling is completed.
The GBA had invited objections to the proposed tree felling on September 20, providing a 10-day deadline. However, the authority did not upload the list of tree species, prompting activists to demand an extension.
According to GBA sources, more than 700 objections were received during the first window, with the remaining submissions coming in before the final deadline.
An officer told The Hindu that the key concerns raised in the objections related to species diversity and the large number of trees proposed to be felled. “Many objections are very detailed and include lists of species to highlight biodiversity. Others focus on a specific aspect, such as the microclimate, and elaborate on the impact that tree felling could have on it,” the officer said.
Biodiversity loss and more
According to the officer, several objections also relate to the size of certain trees, based on independent assessments carried out by those who submitted them. Other objections raise concerns about the impact on biodiversity, hydrological issues arising from the alignment’s proximity to Hebbal Lake, and the risk of the area turning into a heat island, given its role as a key lung space.
The officer said the objections were being filtered and grouped under different themes. “We will forward all the objections and concerns raised by citizens to the tree expert committee and the implementing agency, the BDA. The BDA will also examine the objections and explain why the trees need to be felled. A joint inspection of the site will be carried out by members of the tree expert committee and the BDA to review the proposal,” he said.
Meanwhile, following an NGT stay order, the BDA cannot fell any trees until December 15, the next date of hearing. Any further action will depend on the outcome of the hearing.
Tree committee to decide
Recently, during an interaction with The Hindu, BDA Chairperson N.A. Haris said that only 56 trees would be felled and the remaining trees would be translocated. However, the GBA officer clarified that any decision regarding the trees would have to be taken by the tree expert committee.
“Irrespective of whether the trees are translocated or felled, the BDA will have to plant 10 trees for every tree cleared,” the GBA official said.

briefs.headline: University of Manchester plans centre in Bengaluru to help Indian students find jobs in India
briefs.deck: Engineering, computer science, and business studies are popular among Indian students at the university, followed by programmes in social sciences and humanities
briefs.bodyText:
The University of Manchester will soon open its new centre for the first time in India, in Bengaluru. The centre is expected to facilitate opportunities for students to study at its campus in the U.K. and also help Indian students studying there to seek job opportunities and internships, said Duncan Ivison, Vice-Chancellor, University of Manchester.
Speaking to The Hindu on Friday, Prof. Ivison, who was in the city, said, “The proposed centre will facilitate the academic journey of aspiring Indian students to study at the University of Manchester. Our aim is to also help those who are currently pursuing higher education at our university find jobs and internships back in India. This centre will help create those connections with industry partners, various educational institutions and government agencies.”
He added, “We also aim to connect students aspiring to become entrepreneurs with people who can fund their startups.”
While noting that the university has centres in China, Singapore, Dubai, and Hong Kong, Prof. Ivison said, “Our recent meetings with alumni in Delhi, Bengaluru, and Mumbai have been fruitful. I have been taking insights from them to understand the job scenario and industry demands in India.”
He said there are 50,000 students at their campus, and about one-third of them already have some form of work experience or internship, or are doing entrepreneurial activity.
Besides the international centre, the varsity is also partnering with The Science Gallery in Bengaluru. Prof. Ivison said, “Our partnership with the founders of The Science Gallery aims to combine Art, Culture, and STEM education to introduce it to students, researchers, and people. I believe that art and culture of one society can help us find answers to the most complicated problems apart from Science and Technology.”
Recently, the University’s Manchester Museum signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the gallery.
Popular programmes among Indian students in UK
Prof. Ivison said engineering, computer science and business studies are still popular programmes among Indian students at the university, followed by programmes in social sciences and humanities.
The University of Manchester also has a close relationship with the Indian Institute of Science (IISc). He said, “We offer a joint PhD programme with them which has 15 PhD students from India and Manchester working together on various research projects involving AI, clean energy, quantum technology, life sciences, translating discoveries in life sciences into solutions that can help cure cancer, healthy ageing and more.”

stories.headline: HDFC Bank probes 2 executives for leak of sensitive information
stories.deck: The bank confirmed that an internal probe was underway. “In line with our policies, a review is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts. To protect the integrity of the process and the privacy of all parties involved, we do not comment on active internal reviews,” the bank said.
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: HDFC Bank is investigating whether two executives shared unpublished price sensitive information (UPSI) with outsiders in violation of Sebi regulations and the bank’s code of conduct. UPSI can include data on financial results, dividends, capital raising and the appointment of key managerial personnel. The probe comes as the bank prepares for a leadership change, with incoming MD & CEO Anup Bagchi set to take charge on Oct 27, a day after Sashidhar Jagdishan steps down.
The bank confirmed that an internal probe was under way. “In line with our policies, a review is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts. To protect the integrity of the process and the privacy of all parties involved, we do not comment on active internal reviews,” the bank said.
The bank confirmed that an internal probe was under way.
Info leak: HDFC execs may face regulatory action
Employees can face regulatory action not only for sharing UPSI but also for trading in a company’s shares while in possession of such information. Sebi recently issued an administrative warning to Reliance Industries Ltd’ compliance officer after an investigation into trades between June and Aug 2024 found that two employees and an immediate relative had traded in the company’s shares while in possession of UPSI.
 The Securities Appellate Tribunal upheld Sebi’s insider trading penalties against a former employee of Nucleus Software who had shared advance information about the company’s “huge profits” with a relative.
Bloomberg first reported the investigation into the alleged leaks. According to the report, the executives oversee key businesses and functions at HDFC Bank. The bank identified them during an internal investigation launched after some senior leaders grew concerned about possible information leaks, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter. The probe is continuing as the bank examines whether the information was misused, according to the report.

stories.headline: SBI confirms data leak, says 4,000 customer records identified on dark web
stories.deck: The disclosure follows a claim by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse that a threat actor using the name Siriusim had leaked documents and personal data allegedly linked to SBI. The post claimed the dataset contained 3,75,000 rows in CSV files and 2,722 PDF documents, including customer information, loan applications, supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses.
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: SBI has confirmed a data breach involving 3,897 customer records containing personal information, which were found on the dark web.
SBI identified the records containing personal information in a preliminary analysis of 3.75 lakh records found on the dark web.
The bank said it had activated its cyber incident response protocols and commissioned an independent cybersecurity agency to investigate the incident after receiving alerts from its threat intelligence service provider, Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In on Oct 16.
The disclosure follows a claim by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse that a threat actor using the name Siriusim had leaked documents and personal data allegedly linked to SBI. The post claimed the dataset contained 3,75,000 rows in CSV files and 2,722 PDF documents, including customer information, loan applications, supporting documents, account-opening forms and addresses.
Independent assessment is under way: SBI
The authenticity and full extent of the alleged exposure had not been independently verified in the post.
In its notice to stock exchanges, SBI said the preliminary analysis had identified records containing customers’ registered mobile numbers, dates of birth, names, gender, email addresses, residential addresses, branch and customer information file (CIF) identifiers, lead IDs and metadata associated with loan and lead records. 
The leak of PII can lead to impersonation, loan and benefit frauds and existing account takeovers.
The bank said a detailed investigation was needed to establish the authenticity and completeness of the exposed data, determine its source and extent, and assess the risks to customers and the bank. It has engaged a cybersecurity agency empanelled by CERT-In, India’s national cyber incident response agency, to conduct an independent assessment. SBI said the incident had no material impact on its core business operations, financial performance or business continuity, adding that its core functions continued to operate normally. It said the assessment was underway and remedial and preventive measures were being implemented.

stories.headline: HDFC Bank initiates internal probe into alleged data leak by two senior executives
stories.deck: In line with the bank's policies, the spokesperson said, an internal review into this matter is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts
stories.bodyText:
HDFC Bank has initiated an internal enquiry into the alleged leak of confidential information of the country's biggest private sector lender by two senior executives.
According to sources, the internal review was initiated after senior executives flagged concerns over potential information leaks.
Investigators are examining whether the information disclosed was misused, sources said.
Acknowledging an internal review on the matter, a spokesperson of HDFC Bank said, "The bank is committed to upholding the highest standards of ethics and governance as outlined in our Code of Conduct. We take any report of potential violations seriously."
In line with the bank's policies, the spokesperson said, an internal review into this matter is currently underway to gather and evaluate all relevant facts.
"To protect the integrity of the process and the privacy of all parties involved, we do not comment on active internal reviews. Appropriate action will be taken based on the findings, once the review is complete," the spokesperson added.
The probe comes a week before former head of ICICI Prudential Life Anup Bagchi takes charge as the MD and CEO of the systemically important lender. He is going to be the first outsider to become the head of the bank.
Mr. Bagchi, will succeed Sashidhar Jagdishan, who informed the board in August that he would not seek reappointment when his term ends on October 26.
Mr. Jagdishan took over as the CEO of the bank in 2020 from Aditya Puri, who had led the bank since its inception in 1995.
Within months, it announced the merger of its mortgage major parent, HDFC, with itself, leading to huge expansion in the asset book and worries over business performance, HDFC liability payouts and compressed net interest margins of the combined entity.
The issue of Mr. Jagdishan's reappointment has been a subject of intense speculation, especially after the surprising resignation of non-executive chairman Atanu Chakraborty in March this year, citing concerns on ethics and governance practices at the lender.
In late July, the bank board found shortcomings in the deposit arrangements with the Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC) and also slapped a fine of ₹1 lakh each on Jagdishan and other key executives, even though it said that their actions were not mala fide.
It was alleged that the bank paid, over and above the card rate, for getting high-value deposits from the state-run body and routed them as marketing spends.
Besides, the bank has also faced allegations of mis-selling Credit Suisse's AT-1 bonds to diaspora clients from its Dubai DIFC branch, which led the local regulator to prohibit the bank from onboarding new customers or conducting new business last year.

briefs.headline: RBI rejects all 224 bids in treasury-bill auctions
briefs.deck: Due to a tight fund-flow situation in the system, on the back of a high govt balance, GST-related outflows and funds getting blocked primarily in the Jio Platforms IPO, bidders wanted higher rates in the auction, bond market players said. On the other hand, RBI was reluctant to pay high rates because this could have indicated elevated rate signalling for the short term by the central bank.
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: For the first time since March 2025, 
RBI
 on Wednesday rejected all the 224 bids in the three treasury-bill (T-bill) auctions through which govt was set to borrow Rs 23,000 crore.
Due to a tight fund-flow situation in the system, on the back of a high govt balance, GST-related outflows and funds getting blocked primarily in the Jio Platforms IPO, bidders wanted higher rates in the auction, bond market players said.
On the other hand, RBI was reluctant to pay high rates because this could have indicated elevated rate signalling for the short term by the central bank. What helped RBI’s cause was the high cash balance with govt which was at about Rs 5.3 lakh crore. With govt flush with cash and not in immediate need of funds, RBI could afford to reject all bids in the T-bill auction, a bond dealer said. This decision by the central bank gels well with its policy narrative of ‘calibrated tightening’.
In Wednesday’s auction, RBI had received 77 bids for 91-day T-bills worth Rs 8,000 crore, 68 bids for 182-day T-bills and 79 bids for 364-day T-bills.

briefs.headline: Rate hike: RBI more hawkish than external members at meet
briefs.deck: RBI’s MPC voted unanimously to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%, but split 4-2 on shifting to calibrated tightening, signalling rate cuts were off the table in the near term as inflation threatens to spread beyond food and fuel. Governor Sanjay Malhotra, deputy governor Poonam Gupta, executive director Indranil Bhattacharyya and external member Saugata Bhattacharya backed the shift.
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: The Oct Monetary Policy Committee minutes show that the governor and RBI members were more hawkish than the two external members, who favoured retaining the ‘neutral’ stance rather than shifting to ‘calibrated tightening’, arguing that inflation was driven predominantly by supply-side factors.
RBI’s MPC voted unanimously to raise the 
repo rate
 by 25 basis points to 5.5%, but split 4-2 on shifting to calibrated tightening, signalling rate cuts were off the table in the near term as inflation threatens to spread beyond food and fuel. Governor Sanjay Malhotra, deputy governor Poonam Gupta, executive director Indranil Bhattacharyya and external member Saugata Bhattacharya backed the shift. External members Nagesh Kumar and Ram Singh favoured retaining the neutral stance, citing supply-driven inflation and growth risks.
Calibrated tightening signals that “rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving circumstances and the outlook,” Malhotra said. The duration and extent of any rate-hiking cycle would depend on underlying inflation, the spread of price pressures, second-round effects of supply shocks and demand conditions.
“While inflation is driven largely by supply-side factors and does not show any signs of overheating of the economy nor of generalisation, it is important to manage inflationary expectations,” Kumar said. He favoured a 25-basis-point rate hike but said a neutral stance remained appropriate amid geopolitical and trade policy uncertainties.
Singh warned that shifting to calibrated tightening could signal an extended rate-hiking cycle and undermine the benefits of recent growth-supportive monetary and fiscal policies.

briefs.headline: Security flaw: eMudhra shares take a hit, fall 20%
briefs.deck: The flaw occurred during a key-generation ceremony on April 30, 2025, when a second set of weak keys was generated alongside the original strong keys. Mozilla cryptography engineer Dennis Jackson reported the issue on Oct 17, flagging insufficient randomness that made the keys vulnerable to recovery. eMudhra said it was investigating the root cause.
briefs.bodyText:
BANGLURU/ NEW DELHI: Bengaluru-based digital trust and cybersecurity company eMudhra has acknowledged a cryptographic flaw that generated weak private keys linked to eight intermediate digital certificates in its global website-certificate business, potentially allowing attackers to impersonate legitimate websites. Shares fell 20% on BSE.
The company said the affected TLS business accounts for around 1% of its revenue.
eMudhra reported FY26 revenue of about Rs 710 crore and EBITDA of roughly Rs 110 crore. It had guided for revenue growth of 15–18%, with greater emphasis on higher-margin enterprise solutions.
The flaw occurred during a key-generation ceremony on April 30, 2025, when a second set of weak keys was generated alongside the original strong keys. Mozilla cryptography engineer Dennis Jackson reported the issue on Oct 17, flagging insufficient randomness that made the keys vulnerable to recovery. eMudhra said it was investigating the root cause.
Shares fell 20% on BSE.
eMudhra said it was working with affected customers to replace Transport Layer Security (TLS) certificates and prevent disruption. Co-founder Kaushik Srinivasan told TOI that no certificates had been issued from the affected root in India and that only one US customer had received certificates under the affected infrastructure. 
The company said its infrastructure had not been breached and its Indian digital signature certificate (DSC), eSign and enterprise solutions businesses remained unaffected.
Govt officials said the ministry of electronics and IT has taken serious note of the incident with a special team constituted to investigate the matter.
“The impact of this incident on Indian websites and applications have been very limited and for a very short interval… Important to note that Digital Signature Certificates and eSign services regulated by Controller of Certifying Authorities, remain completely unaffected by this incident,” an official said.
Mozilla blocked six affected certificates, released Firefox security updates and removed the relevant root certificate from its trust store. Google blocked the affected public keys, extending protection to supported Android devices, while Cloudflare introduced safeguards. Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) warned that compromised keys could enable website impersonation, interception of communications and the issuance of fraudulent code-signing certificates that make malicious software appear legitimate. It advised organisations to install the latest security patches.

briefs.headline: At 7.9%, core sector clocks fastest growth in new series
